arm_c_atomic_full_budget.prompt_note: Generated under the original wording ('use most of that budget'). The profile has since been retargeted to ~900 words with a hard 1,024 ceiling; these numbers predate that change.

arm_d_focused_citations.change: Removed the 'cite every reference' instruction; told the model to cite the single best supporting document and add more only if each independently supports the object.
arm_d_focused_citations.pipeline_change: Added trim_to_word_limit and normalize_generated_record, so the word cap and the all-cited rule are enforced deterministically instead of by prompt.

caveats: Four topics; consistent direction but not a significance test.
Generation is high variance: the same default config produced 9 and then 28 answer objects for topic 58 in different runs.
Judge changed from gpt-5.5 to DeepSeek V4 Flash, so absolute values are not comparable across records; the A/B contrast within this record is consistent.
Automated assignment scores above NIST manual assignment.

citation_count_effect.description: Full Support rate collapses as citations per object rise; measured on arm C.
citation_count_effect.mechanism: The all-cited rule forced long reference lists to be covered by padding two or three citations onto nearly every object; trailing citations frequently do not support the claim.

eliminated.effort_max: No better than high; 3/4 topics, one lost to a fabricated citation index.
eliminated.model_version: deepseek-v4-flash was a superseded 2026-04-24 preview; 0731 is newer and cheaper.
eliminated.provider_routing: structured_output json_object failed 3/4 topics with malformed shapes, so the strict schema is load-bearing and the third-party-routing hypothesis is disproved.
eliminated.reasoning_effort: OpenRouter's medium is not a native DeepSeek level and spent roughly half the token budget on reasoning, causing 397-676 word answers. Native high fixed length entirely.
eliminated.vendor_json_example: DeepSeek documents that JSON output needs a worked in-prompt example. Adding one made compliance worse, 59% to 26% single-citation, with shorter answers and one failure.

deepseek_configuration_sweep.purpose: Establish whether the DeepSeek coverage gap was configuration or capability.
deepseek_configuration_sweep.remaining: Instruction placement, which the tail contract addresses and which recovered most of the gap.
deepseek_configuration_sweep.support_note: DeepSeek 0731 beats Sol's focused_citations arm on citation support (hard precision 0.678 against 0.481) while trailing on coverage, so it is not uniformly worse.

design: Four development topics generated under both prompt profiles. Retrieval, generator model and judge held fixed. Judge is DeepSeek V4 Flash for every cell.

budget_frontier.description: Passage budget trades coverage against citation precision; extraction dominates truncation at every point tested.
budget_frontier.reading: Less but better-selected text makes the model assert less and ground it better. Where to sit depends on how organizers weight coverage against support, which is not observable.

extractive_passage_selection.change: dev_rag_inputs --passage-words replaces the generator's head truncation with query-relevant window selection (120-word windows, scored by distinct narrative-term coverage, greedy non-overlapping, re-emitted in document order).
extractive_passage_selection.conclusion: Extraction buys a 2.4x cost reduction and substantially better citation support for 0.057 strict_vital of coverage. It is a genuine trade rather than the free win predicted; a larger passage budget is the untested middle ground.

matched_budget_test.cost_correction: Extraction at full budget costs slightly more, not less: $0.7882 against $0.7115. Fewer document words are offset by longer answers, and output tokens dominate. Only reducing the budget saves money.
matched_budget_test.finding: At matched budget extraction beats truncation on four of five metrics: coverage +0.025, weighted precision +0.025, hard precision +0.025, No Support 9.6% to 7.4%, all-coverage level. No single delta clears the four-topic noise bar, but the direction is consistent across independent metrics. The 0.057 coverage loss in the first comparison came from the budget cut, not the selection method.
matched_budget_test.purpose: Isolate selection method from budget. The first comparison changed both at once and could not attribute the coverage loss.

extractive_passage_selection.measurement_error_corrected: The extractive arm was first judged against the head-truncated document text rather than the passages its generator actually read, producing an artificial 32.7% No Support rate and an incorrect conclusion that extraction hurt support. Re-judging against matched evidence reversed it.
extractive_passage_selection.outstanding_caveat: Each arm is now judged against its own evidence view, which is internally consistent but not what organizers do: they resolve citations from the index, i.e. full documents. Judging both arms against full document text is the realistic measurement and is untested.

four_arm_summary.caveat: Four topics. Generation variance alone has produced 9 versus 28 objects for the same config, so coverage differences of this size are not resolved.
four_arm_summary.recommendation: Arm D. It wins every citation-support metric both as generated and at the oracle repair ceiling, and because every object carries exactly one citation its wp_all equals wp_first by construction, so it cannot be diluted on the all-judged variant. It gives up 0.047 strict_vital against arm A for +0.217 weighted precision and +0.410 hard precision.

generation_reliability.implication: About one topic in four fails first time. Over 119 topics that is ~30 resumes at $0.71 each.
generation_reliability.note: Uncited-reference failures are self-imposed; the guidelines state uncited references do not hurt the score.

generation_reliability_arm_d.note: Normalization eliminated the uncited-reference mode entirely. The word cap became the dominant failure, which is why a deterministic trim was added.

generator_model_sweep.conclusion: No cheaper model substitutes for Sol. Single-citation compliance tracks citation support almost monotonically (100% -> 9.6% No Support, 54% -> 34.3%, 26% -> 22.9%), and Sol is the only model that complied fully. Two models fabricated document ids outside the retrieval pool, which is a correctness failure rather than a formatting one.
generator_model_sweep.design: Arm D prompt and the same four topics for every model; only the generator changed. Judge held at deepseek-v4-flash throughout.
generator_model_sweep.reliability_note: Substitution here is a reliability problem as much as a quality one. The contract stacks strict JSON-schema structured output, reasoning effort and a multi-part formatting instruction; only Sol handled all three across providers. Two models needed max_tokens raised from 6,000 to 32,000 merely to finish, and truncated failures are still billed.

repair_ceiling.description: Dropping every judge-labelled No Support citation, an oracle upper bound.
repair_ceiling.finding: A cheap model with flawless repair only reaches Sol's unrepaired score, and coverage is repair-proof because repair never edits answer text.

deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro.note: Erratic citation compliance; 10 of 34 objects on one topic carried three citations.

google/gemini-3-flash-preview.note: Two topics failed by emitting docids outside the retrieval pool; poor citation compliance on the one that completed.

moonshotai/kimi-k2-thinking.note: Short answers, erratic citations, and one topic failed by emitting a docid outside the retrieval pool.

z-ai/glm-4.7.note: Returns finish_reason stop with completion tokens but null content via DeepInfra; a provider response-shape problem, not max_tokens.

caveats: Four topics, and Sol's gain is uneven: +0.114 on topic 58 and +0.082 on 200, flat on 144, -0.027 on 72.
DeepSeek's tail arm covers three topics; topic 72 failed twice with a non-JSON response and is where its baseline was weakest, so the DeepSeek tail mean is flattered.
findings: Restating the contract after the question helps; moving it into the system message does not. The mechanism is proximity to the generation point, not channel privilege.
The gain transfers across models: Sol +0.042 strict_vital, DeepSeek +0.050. On the shared prompt Sol still leads DeepSeek by 0.081 on the three shared topics.
For Sol the tail contract is a strict improvement on every metric measured, so it replaces focused_citations in the competition config.
Transfer holding for this variant validates screening prompt changes on DeepSeek at 1/53 the cost, but it is one variant; a change targeting a DeepSeek-specific weakness need not transfer.
instruction_placement_and_transfer.hypothesis: With 100 documents inserted the output contract sits roughly 120k tokens above the generation point, a lost-in-the-middle position. Only the question benefits from recency.

variants.contract_in_system: moves the contract into the system message, leaving documents plus question in the user message
variants.focused_citations_tail: restates a compact contract after the question

length.note: Neither arm approaches the cap. Nugget scoring is pure recall with no length penalty.

prompt_document_budget.finding: 91% of documents are truncated and the model sees only 17% of the pool, always the opening words, which on web pages is frequently navigation chrome. Relevance-selected passages should cut cost roughly threefold while improving what the model reads; the window scorer in facet_retrieval.MixedbreadCoverageScorer already exists for this.
prompt_document_budget.pool: 100 documents per topic, truncated to the first 1,000 words each

review_corrections.extraction_is_dev_only: select_passages lives in dev_rag_inputs.py, which reads dev BM25 archives. competition_retrieval does not use it, so extractive selection is not on the competition path and is not proposed for this cycle.
review_corrections.normalizer_hardening: Three defects found and fixed after review: invalid citations were silently pruned rather than reported, disabling an existing range check; duplicate citations survived remapping and failed validation later; and a docid listed at two positions produced two citations of one document. Invalid citations now raise, duplicates collapse, and references canonicalize by docid.
not_shipping: Extractive passage selection: dev-only code path, deltas around 0.025 on four topics, and the 261-word precision figure partly reflects the model being able to echo only what it was shown.
The 261-word budget: a coverage/precision dial set without knowing organizer weighting.
Any generator conclusion beyond 'Sol only': one to four topics per model is anecdote.
review_corrections.one_citation_conclusion_qualified: Partly metric mechanics. RAGDoll's hard_precision and weighted_precision_first_citation judge only citations[0], and weighted_precision_all_judged averages per object, so removing trailing citations improves the averaged metrics arithmetically rather than behaviourally. The 72.5/27.9/11.1 Full Support table also carries a confound: multi-citation objects are disproportionately the fused multi-claim objects no single document can support. What survives is that arm D beat every other arm on wp_first and hard_precision, which trailing citations cannot dilute, so its first citations genuinely improved. Credit belongs to 'cite the single best supporting document', not to capping the count. A second citation that independently supports the claim is free under every metric except the all-judged average, so 'exactly one' should stay prompt guidance and never become a validator rule.
review_corrections.reachability_gap: The measured winner was not reachable by the competition pipeline. No checked-in config set prompt_profile, so a production run would have used the default prompt (arm A, hard precision 0.071) with the new post-processors, a combination never measured. Fixed by setting prompt_profile: focused_citations in configs/rag26_competition_rag_gpt_sol_v1.yaml.

supersedes: The two-topic comparison in dev_ragdoll_nugget_eval_spike_v1, which reported atomic as neutral-to-better on coverage.

three_arm_summary.reading: No arm dominates. B has by far the cleanest citations (11% No Support against 30% for both A and C) and the best weighted precision. C recovers most of B's coverage loss and posts the best strict_all and hard_precision, but its citation error rate returns to A's level: pushing length appears to make the model assert more than it can ground.
